figures_added.what: Still-water scene: a kite (amber diamond) 5 m above a horizontal water line and its dashed mirror reflection 5 m below, marked '?'. Theme-safe (text/strokes currentColor, water rect soft blue fill-opacity 0.18, viewBox + role=img + aria-label). Supports the opener's reflection box (answer -5) introducing -f(x) as reflection in the x-axis.

Chart.js y=x^2 (blue) and y=-x^2 (orange), x from -3 to 3. The exam figure for '-f(x) is a reflection in which axis': every orange y is the negation of the blue y (verified), showing the reflection in the x-axis.
Chart.js y=x^2 (blue) and y=x^2-5 (orange), x from -3 to 3. Shows the translation by vector (0,-5): every plotted orange point is 5 below the blue (verified), so the constant term is -5.
Chart.js y=x^2 (blue, x -3..3) and y=(x-3)^2+5 (orange, x 0..6). Shows the vertex moving from (0,0) to (3,5): right 3, up 5. Every plotted point satisfies its equation (verified).

notes: Point-on-y=f(x) problems (abstract f, given point in text) got no figure, matching the exam, which states the point in words rather than printing a graph. Figures added only where the exam prints one: the concrete y=x^2 problems (silver[4], gold[4]), the reflection concept (silver[3], using an asymmetric-in-y curve so the flip is visible), and the opener scene. f(-x) MC (silver[6]) deliberately got no chart: reflecting y=x^2 in the y-axis is invisible, so a figure would mislead. All figures theme-safe; no external refs.
